title: Gen
identity: Ryo Noda’s Gen is the author’s piano transcription of his alto saxophone concerto, Leduc AL27329. The Philharmonie de Paris guide gives an approximate 18-minute duration and reports a high altissimo E-flat; Wise Music lists 15 minutes for the orchestral work, so the duration figures are version/source specific.

evidence.claim: Leduc AL27329 is a reduction for alto saxophone and piano of Noda's concerto.
A retailer identifies the 24-page Leduc AL27329 edition.

The Philharmonie de Paris digitized guide identifies Leduc AL27329 as the author’s piano transcription of the alto saxophone concerto, about 18 minutes, and reports a highest note of written E-flat in the altissimo register. This is secondary pedagogical description, not a notation inspection.
evidence.source_name: Philharmonie de Paris, 10 ans avec le saxophone, printed p. 116

review_focus: The guide reports an altissimo E-flat and substantial piano ensemble work; inspect the reduction for the exact register, coordination, and how orchestral roles are redistributed.
gaps: No readable notation for the piano reduction was inspected, so the exact written range and later-section demands remain unverified.
Duration differs by source/version: the guide gives about 18 minutes for the reduction and Wise lists 15 minutes for the orchestral work.
No verified performance recording of the piano reduction was located.
